--- title: "[PiecewiseExponential]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Piecewise exponential survival model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/feat-ml/greenwood/_pem.py#L181-L599){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python PiecewiseExponential( *, breaks=None, knot_strategy="aic", max_knots=10, conf_level=0.95 ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Assumes the hazard is constant within each time interval but can differ between intervals. Covariates enter multiplicatively (proportional hazards within each interval). The model is fit by maximum likelihood, equivalent to a Poisson GLM on the interval-expanded dataset with `log(exposure)` as offset. This sits between the fully nonparametric Cox model and the fully parametric AFT: it estimates the baseline hazard but restricts it to a step function. Fewer intervals give a smoother hazard. More intervals approach the Cox model's flexibility. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [breaks]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[float] | tuple[float, ...] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Time points at which the hazard is allowed to change. For example, `breaks=[180, 365]` creates three intervals: `(0, 180]`, `(180, 365]`, and `(365, inf]`. When `None` (default), knots are chosen automatically by minimizing AIC. [knot_strategy]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["aic"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Strategy for automatic knot selection when `breaks` is `None`. `"aic"` (default) minimizes the Akaike information criterion. `"bic"` minimizes the Bayesian information criterion. Ignored when `breaks` is provided. [max_knots]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of interior knots to consider during automatic selection (the default is `10`). Ignored when `breaks` is provided. [conf_level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence level for coefficient intervals (the default is `0.95`). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#5d37ec86 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") y = gw.Surv.right(lung["time"], event=(lung["status"] == 2)) pem = gw.PiecewiseExponential().fit(y, lung[["age", "sex"]]) pem ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` PiecewiseExponential (1 intervals) coef se(coef) z p age 0.01562 0.009106 1.715 0.0863 sex -0.4809 0.1671 -2.878 0.003999 Intervals: (0, inf] n = 228, events = 165 Log-likelihood = -281.9 AIC = 569.7 ``` ::: ::: With manual break points: ::: {#28f954d3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} pem_manual = gw.PiecewiseExponential(breaks=[180, 365]).fit(y, lung[["age", "sex"]]) pem_manual.to_frame(format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

### [baseline_hazard()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return the piecewise-constant baseline hazard as a DataFrame. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/feat-ml/greenwood/_pem.py#L452-L488){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python baseline_hazard(*, format=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each row gives the interval boundaries and the constant hazard rate within that interval. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None`, `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pandas.DataFrame, polars.DataFrame, or pyarrow.Table]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#d3c36068 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") y = gw.Surv.right(lung["time"], event=(lung["status"] == 2)) pem = gw.PiecewiseExponential(breaks=[180, 365]).fit(y, lung[["age", "sex"]]) pem.baseline_hazard(format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
